name: Risograph print
summary: A print from a stencil duplicator: a thermal head cuts a master and the drum pushes soy ink through it, one drum and one bright spot colour for each layer. Riso Kagaku sold it for schools and offices from 1986; from the 2000s, studios made its grain and misregister an art look.

philosophy.core_thesis: Bright spot inks that mix where they overlap, with a soft grain and a small shift, give a cheap print the warmth of a hand process.
design_principles: Separate the image into 2–4 spot colours; draw each layer in black as a separate file.
Use the bright riso inks: fluorescent pink, medium blue, yellow, and others from the drum list.
Overprint the transparent inks to make the third and fourth colours (pink over yellow gives orange).
Use a grain screen at 50–110 lines an inch for the tones; avoid large flat solids, which print unevenly.
Accept a shift of 1–2 mm between the layers; design so that a small gap does not break the image.
Print on an uncoated, slightly warm paper that takes the soy ink.
anti_patterns: Process CMYK colour that hides the spot inks
Large, heavy solids that smear and set off
Exact register needed for small text in two colours

process.matrix: A thermal master cut on the machine, wrapped on a drum of soy ink.
process.press: A Riso digital duplicator, one or two drums at a pass, up to 150 sheets a minute.
process.image_making: The designer separates the layers in software; the printer changes the drum for each colour and feeds the sheets again.
process.edition: 50–2,000 copies; above that, offset costs less.

inks.strategy: Spot colours from the riso drum list, each one transparent, so overprints mix.

colours.name: Medium blue
colours.role: the key layer and the darks

colours.name: Fluorescent pink
colours.role: warm accents and orange with yellow

screening.rule: Make the tone with the grain (FM) screen of the duplicator or a coarse halftone of 50–110 lines an inch.

registration.rule: Each drum pass can shift 1–2 mm; the misregister is part of the look.

substrate.stock: An uncoated paper, often recycled, with a soft surface for the soy ink.
substrate.finish: Uncoated, with a slight tooth; natural white or cream.

surface.impression: No bite; the ink sinks into the paper.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a slight chalky softness; fluorescent inks glow.
surface.texture: A soft grain in the tones, uneven solids and roller marks.

emotion.target_response: Warm, playful craft: the viewer feels a small studio print, bright and a little imperfect.

avoid_when: The design depends on exact register of small text.

modifiers.how: Change the riso drum for a hand screen; use opaque inks and a coarse halftone.
Print in black only on a copier and paste the layout by hand.
